messages:
maria: Quick question — observed a few requests where X-Project-ID was missing and the request still succeeded but got billed/attributed to the org fallback. Is that expected behavior? @ben can you confirm?

ben: Yeah — ingress lookup order is: X-Project-ID -> X-Org -> API-Key mapping. We kept org fallback for compat so clients without project header don't break.

ashok: Security concern: silent fallback can mask auth intent and cause billing/permission surprises. For write endpoints we should probably reject if project header absent but API key could map to multiple projects.

maria: Product wants stricter behavior for mutating endpoints (create/update/delete). Read-only endpoints ok to be lenient. Would prefer a clear 4xx instead of silently falling back.

ben: Implementation note: we have a feature flag `strict_project_header` per-route. Default was off. We can flip it for /v1/models/* POST/PUT/DELETE.

levan: Infra: flipping flag per-route is straightforward, but need a rollout window and metrics. Also ensure key-rotation storm doesn't spike error rates.

maria: I opened PR #4823 — adds middleware option and a migration guide. Pinged reviewers: @ben @ashok.

ben: Taking a look now. Quick question: should missing header return 401 (unauth) or 403 (forbidden)?

ashok: If API key is valid but project header is required and absent, 403 makes sense: the caller is authenticated but not authorized for that project. If key missing or invalid -> 401.

jess: Product thumbs up for 403 on writes. Also want clear error body so integrators can auto-fix: {"error":"missing_project_header","hint":"include X-Project-ID or use project-scoped key"}.

maria: Good call. Ben — can we add that JSON error shape to the contract doc? Also add a migration note about toggle.

ben: Yes. I'll update openapi and add an example response. Example snippet in middleware:

```
if (route.enforceProjectHeader && !req.headers['x-project-id']) {
  return res.status(403).json({ error: 'missing_project_header', hint: 'include X-Project-ID or use project-scoped key' });
}
```

levan: We'll want telemetry: metric `auth.missing_project_header.count` and tag by route and org. Deploy team please add to runbook for alerting.

deploy-bot: deploy queued — staging middleware-change branch -> staging (pr-4823). ETA 12m.

sre-bot: info: observed 27 requests in last 1h with missing X-Project-ID to write endpoints (staging test).

maria: Thanks. Two rollout asks: 1) start in staging + smoke tests, 2) 48h canary on a subset of traffic, 3) automatic fallback to old behavior if error rate > 1% for 5m.

ben: I wired canary flagging in the PR. Also included toggle endpoint to switch per-route.

ashok: Add audit log entry when enforcement rejects — include request id, api key id, inferred org. We need that for investigations.

maria: Agreed. Ben — add audit log and the exact 403 payload to the PR, then I can merge and schedule canary.

ben: Will do. ETA today EOD.

jess: I'll update integrator docs & notify partners about upcoming stricter behavior for writes.

maria: Thanks everyone. Action items: Ben: update PR with error shape + audit log + openapi. Levan: prepare metrics/dashboards and canary rollout plan. Ashok: sign-off on error semantics. Jess: customer comms. I'll follow up once PR is staged. :thumbsup:

ben: Reviewing now :eyes:

ashok: LGTM on semantics, will give final sign-off after audit log is present.

maria: Cool — closing loop here, will post canary start time in #eng-releases.
